title: Visiting Lumen Valley Observatory and its four telescopes
body: Posted 12 May 2019. Last weekend we drove up Halden Ridge to the Lumen Valley Observatory. The observatory operates four telescopes: the 2.4 m Aster reflector, the 1.0 m Meridian survey telescope, a 0.6 m solar telescope and the historic 0.5 m Founders refractor from 1961. Night tours run Fridays. Bring a jacket, the ridge gets cold even in summer. The visitor centre sells hot chocolate and the ticket desk closes at 9 pm.

title: Lumen Valley Observatory - Wikipedia
body: The Lumen Valley Observatory is an astronomical observatory on Halden Ridge, founded in 1961 by the Lumen Valley Astronomical Society. It operates several optical telescopes and hosts a public visitor centre. The observatory expanded its facilities in 2022 and again in 2024. The number of visitors has grown steadily since the opening of the new planetarium. See the official site for the current list of facilities and opening hours.

title: Facilities | Lumen Valley Observatory
body: Updated January 2026. Our facilities on Halden Ridge comprise six research and outreach instruments: the 2.4 m Aster reflector (1988), the 1.0 m Meridian survey instrument (2003), the 0.6 m Helios solar instrument (2010), the 0.5 m Founders refractor (1961), the 1.2 m Corvid near-infrared instrument commissioned in 2022, and the 0.8 m Pallas robotic instrument commissioned in 2024. All six are in regular operation. The planetarium (opened 2023) is not a telescope.

title: Tickets and opening hours | Lumen Valley Observatory
body: Standard admission (from 1 March 2025): Adult SGD 18, Concession SGD 12, Child under 6 free. Before 1 March 2025 the adult price was SGD 15. Night tours are an additional SGD 10. Open Tuesday to Sunday 10:00 to 21:00, closed Mondays and public holidays. Group bookings of 15 or more receive a 10 percent discount on request.

title: Observatory raises ticket prices for first time in a decade - Halden Herald
body: Published 20 February 2025. The Lumen Valley Observatory will raise its standard adult ticket from SGD 15 to SGD 18 on 1 March, the first increase since 2015. The adult ticket price of SGD 15 has been unchanged for ten years, a spokesperson said. Visitor numbers in 2024 reached 38,900, up from 35,200 in 2023, driven by the new planetarium. The observatory said its Friday night tours drew 8,400 participants last year and expects a similar number in 2025. The observatory reports on a financial year running April to March; its preliminary count for financial year 2024/25 was about 40,100 visitors, the spokesperson added.

title: Annual Visitor Report 2025 | Lumen Valley Observatory
body: Total visitors in calendar year 2025: 42,310 (2024: 38,900; 2023: 35,200). Monthly breakdown 2025: Jan 2,980; Feb 2,760; Mar 3,410; Apr 3,620; May 3,540; Jun 4,210; Jul 4,630; Aug 4,480; Sep 3,390; Oct 3,210; Nov 2,940; Dec 3,140. Night tour participants (included in the total): 6,120. School groups (included in the total): 7,850. All figures are counts of admitted persons.

title: Halden Ridge weather and stargazing conditions
body: Posted 3 March 2023. Halden Ridge sits at 1,420 m. The observatory's newest instrument, the 1.2 m Corvid near-infrared telescope commissioned in 2022, is not open to the public but you can see its dome from the car park. The best months for stargazing are June to September when the valley fog stays below the ridge. The observatory publishes a nightly seeing forecast. Temperatures drop to 4 C at night even in July.

title: Lumen Valley Astronomical Society - history
body: The society was founded in 1958 and opened the Lumen Valley Observatory in 1961 with a single 0.5 m refractor, the Founders telescope. Over the decades the society and later the observatory trust added further telescopes. The society continues to run the Friday night tours in partnership with the observatory.

title: Annual Visitor Report 2024 | Lumen Valley Observatory
body: Total visitors in calendar year 2024: 38,900 (2023: 35,200). Monthly breakdown 2024: Jan 2,610; Feb 2,480; Mar 3,050; Apr 3,220; May 3,180; Jun 3,860; Jul 4,310; Aug 4,120; Sep 3,090; Oct 2,980; Nov 2,730; Dec 3,270. Night tour participants (included in the total): 5,480. All figures are counts of admitted persons.

title: Governance and reporting | Lumen Valley Observatory
body: The Lumen Valley Observatory Trust is a registered charity. Its financial year runs from 1 April to 31 March; the annual accounts for financial year 2024/25 cover 1 April 2024 to 31 March 2025. Visitor statistics are published per calendar year in the Annual Visitor Reports. Director: Dr. Ilse Varga (since 2019). Previous director: Prof. Tomas Reinholt (2004-2019).

title: Pallas robotic telescope declared operational - Lumen Valley Observatory news
body: 3 September 2024. The 0.8 m Pallas robotic instrument was declared fully operational today, ending its commissioning campaign. Pallas achieved first light on 14 May 2024. It is the observatory's sixth instrument and joins Corvid (2022) in the automated survey programme. Director Dr. Ilse Varga thanked the engineering team.

title: A summer on the ridge: commissioning Pallas
body: Posted 20 October 2024. I volunteered during the Pallas commissioning, which took about three months over the summer of 2024, from first light in May until the formal sign-off in September. The 0.8 m robotic telescope now runs on its own every clear night. Fun fact: the dome was painted twice.

title: Lumen Valley Public Observatory - home
body: Welcome to the Lumen Valley Public Observatory on Dunmore Hill, run by volunteers since 1994. We are not affiliated with the Lumen Valley Observatory on Halden Ridge. Free public viewing every Saturday night. Our telescopes: a 0.4 m Dobsonian reflector (our largest), a 0.25 m Schmidt-Cassegrain and a 0.15 m refractor for solar viewing.

title: Lumen Valley Public Observatory - telescopes
body: Three telescopes are available to visitors: the 0.4 m 'Big Dob' Dobsonian reflector built by members in 2001, a 0.25 m Schmidt-Cassegrain on a go-to mount, and a 0.15 m hydrogen-alpha solar refractor. The 0.4 m instrument is the largest telescope at the Public Observatory.

title: Lumen Valley Observatory - largest telescopes and facilities | Halden tourism
body: The Lumen Valley Observatory is the valley's main attraction for stargazers. Its largest telescope is the 2.4 m Aster reflector, and the site also has a planetarium, a cafe and a gift shop. Do not confuse it with the smaller Lumen Valley Public Observatory run by the amateur club on Dunmore Hill.

title: Lumen Valley Wine Route - Observatory Deck
body: The Observatory Deck at Karsten Estate winery offers views over the Lumen Valley vineyards and, on clear nights, of the domes on Halden Ridge. Tastings from SGD 25. The deck has a 0.2 m telescope for guests. Open Thursday to Sunday.

title: Aster 2.4 m reflector | Lumen Valley Observatory
body: The 2.4 m Aster reflector saw first light in 1988 and remains the largest telescope on Halden Ridge. It is used for spectroscopy of variable stars and, on Friday nights, for public viewing. Major mirror re-aluminisation in 2015.

title: Meridian 1.0 m survey instrument | Lumen Valley Observatory
body: The 1.0 m Meridian survey instrument was commissioned in 2003 and carries a wide-field camera used for asteroid follow-up. It replaced an earlier 0.75 m survey telescope that was decommissioned in 2002 and sold to a university.

title: Helios solar instrument | Lumen Valley Observatory
body: The 0.6 m Helios solar instrument has operated since 2010 and feeds the daily solar images shown in the visitor centre.

title: Founders refractor | Lumen Valley Observatory
body: The 0.5 m Founders refractor is the observatory's original instrument from 1961 and is still used for public viewing and outreach.

title: Corvid near-infrared instrument | Lumen Valley Observatory
body: The 1.2 m Corvid near-infrared instrument was commissioned in 2022 and is operated remotely by the survey team. It is not part of the public tours.

title: Observatory news archive 2019-2023 | Lumen Valley Observatory
body: 2023: planetarium opens (12 August). 2022: Corvid 1.2 m commissioned. 2021: visitor centre refurbished. 2020: site closed March to July. 2019: Dr. Ilse Varga appointed director; the 0.75 m former survey telescope, sold in 2002, is returned on loan for the 60th-anniversary exhibition and displayed (not operated) in the visitor centre.

title: Lumen Valley Astronomical Society - 50th anniversary gala (2008)
body: On 14 June 2008 the Lumen Valley Astronomical Society celebrated fifty years since its founding in 1958 with a gala at the observatory it helped build in 1961. Guests toured the three telescopes then in operation on the ridge.

title: Halden Herald - Observatory marks 60 years (2021)
body: Published 15 June 2021. The Lumen Valley Observatory marked 60 years since its opening in 1961 with an open day. Five telescopes are now on the ridge, the director said, with a sixth, a 1.2 m infrared instrument, due next year. The amateur Lumen Valley Public Observatory on Dunmore Hill also celebrated, offering free viewing through its 0.4 m telescope.

title: Night tours | Lumen Valley Observatory
body: Night tours run every Friday from 20:00 and last two hours; they include the Aster and Founders telescopes and the planetarium. Night tour supplement: SGD 10 on top of standard admission. Capacity 60 per tour. In 2025 we welcomed 6,120 night tour participants.

title: School visits | Lumen Valley Observatory
body: School groups receive the concession rate (SGD 12) and a free teacher place per ten pupils. 7,850 pupils visited in 2025 and 7,110 in 2024. Bookings open each September.

title: Lumen Valley Observatory - TripNotes reviews
body: 4.6 stars from 1,284 reviews. 'Great night tour, the big telescope is amazing' - 'Tickets went up to 18 dollars this year, still worth it' - 'The cafe closes at 8 pm, go before the tour' - 'Four telescopes to look through on the Friday tour' (note: tours visit two of the six instruments).

title: Halden Ridge access road and parking
body: The access road to the Lumen Valley Observatory closes in heavy snow. Parking for 120 cars. A shuttle runs from Halden station on Friday evenings for night tours.

title: Dr. Ilse Varga - staff profile | Lumen Valley Observatory
body: Dr. Ilse Varga has been Director since March 2019. Her research concerns near-infrared variability surveys with Corvid. She previously led the Meridian survey programme from 2011.

title: Lumen Valley Observatory (disambiguation) - Wikipedia
body: Lumen Valley Observatory may refer to: the Lumen Valley Observatory, a research and public observatory on Halden Ridge founded in 1961; the Lumen Valley Public Observatory, an amateur observatory on Dunmore Hill founded in 1994; the Observatory Deck at Karsten Estate winery.
